hero.headline: James Martin wins Democratic primary for Congressional District 21 by less than 1%, will face Brian Mast in November
hero.teaser: Coast Guard veteran James Martin secured the Democratic nomination for Florida's 21st Congressional District Friday after capturing 50.4% of the vote compared t.
hero.body:
Coast Guard veteran James Martin secured the Democratic nomination for Florida's 21st Congressional District Friday after capturing 50.4% of the vote compared to challenger Bernard Taylor's 49.6%, according to election results from NBC News. The narrow margin underscores the competitive nature of the Democratic race in a district that includes St. Lucie County, Martin County and portions of northern Palm Beach County. Martin will now face incumbent Republican Rep. Brian Mast in November's general election.

Taylor conceded the race Thursday night on social media, acknowledging the outcome while emphasizing the importance of democratic processes. "The voters have spoken, and while this isn't the outcome we hoped for, we respect their decision," Taylor wrote on X. "Democracy only works when we respect the voice of the people, even when the result isn't the one we wanted." Martin posted on Facebook Thursday evening that he was "honored to be the nominee" and congratulated Taylor on a "hard-fought race."

Rep. Brian Mast, an Army veteran who has represented the district since 2017, ran unopposed in the Republican primary. A Democrat has not represented this area of Florida in a decade. Both Martin and Mast bring military backgrounds to their campaigns, with Martin's Coast Guard service and Mast's Army experience potentially resonating with the significant veteran population throughout the Treasure Coast region.

Florida's 21st Congressional District spans a significant portion of the Treasure Coast, encompassing communities from northern Palm Beach County through Martin County and into St. Lucie County. With both major party nominees now confirmed, voters in St. Lucie, Martin and northern Palm Beach counties can expect an active campaign season as Martin challenges the incumbent Republican.

cards.headline: Florida SNAP enrollment drops 22% as Trump-backed work requirements take effect
cards.teaser: Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program in Florida fell by more than 22% in a 12-month span as work requirements and other provisions of President Donald Trump'
cards.body:
Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program in Florida fell by more than 22% in a 12-month span as work requirements and other provisions of President Donald Trump's big beautiful bill take hold. The state's Department of Children and Families said in a statement that the decreasing number is reflective of the state's strong focus on advancing opportunities for Floridians and their families to achieve economic self-sufficiency. Nationwide, SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2 million in May 2025 to 36.6 million in May 2026, a drop of more than 13%.

The expanded SNAP work requirement now includes adults ages 55 to 64 and those with children ages 14 to 17. Many adults 54 and younger without minor children have long been required to work to get SNAP benefits. The new law requires most people who previously had been exempt from requirements to either work, volunteer or go to school to get benefits. Those 65 and older or with children younger than 14 remain exempt, as do those with health limitations. Some groups that had been exempted from the requirement, including homeless people, no longer are.

Paco Velez, the president and CEO of Feeding South Florida, said the 22% one-year enrollment drop in Florida is driven partly by immigrants who are in the U.S. legally but fear being targeted by Trump's immigration crackdown if they're seeking government benefits. Advocates say people are losing coverage because they miss deadlines or don't have the needed documentation handy, and that some state agencies that run the programs are overwhelmed trying to keep up with changes. Tia Fields, who analyzes social safety net policies at the advocacy group Invest in Louisiana, said the main reason she's seeing people lose coverage is not failure to meet work requirements but administrative paperwork.

The monthly SNAP benefit, which is delivered on debit cards that can be used only for groceries, is $344 per household on average. Children in households that receive the benefit can be automatically enrolled in free school lunch programs or in the SNAP for Women, Infants and Children program for low-income mothers, young children and expectant parents if they meet the other criteria. Some food banks have ramped up donations to try to meet a demand that has risen as SNAP rolls have declined, but advocates say that isn't expected to bridge the gap fully.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested on eight burglary charges in Port St. Lucie Spanish Lakes community
cards.teaser: Herman Ray Nettles, 44, of Fort Pierce, is in the St. Lucie County Jail on eight counts of burglary of an unoccupied conveyance while unarmed on a $20,000 bond, stemming from incidents in the Spanish Lakes community in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Herman Ray Nettles, 44, of Fort Pierce, was arrested on August 17 following multiple burglaries and attempted burglaries of vehicles in the Spanish Lakes One community in Port St. Lucie. St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office Patrol Operations Bureau deputies responded to multiple calls for service in the community. Working with Patrol Operations Bureau deputies and crime analysts, investigators developed and identified Nettles as a suspect.

St. Lucie County Sheriffs Office Deputy Martinez-Delgado, an off-duty officer, spotted Nettles traveling on U.S. Highway 1 in Port St. Lucie and notified 911. Patrol Operations Bureau deputies responded and detained Nettles before transporting him to the Criminal Investigations Division for further investigation. Probable cause was developed connecting Nettles to all eight incidents.

Nettles is in the St. Lucie County Jail as of August 21 on eight counts of burglary of an unoccupied conveyance while unarmed on a $20,000 bond. Being a law enforcement officer doesn't stop when the shift ends, said Sheriff Richard Del Toro. Deputy Martinez-Delgado's quick recognition and immediate action helped bring this suspect into custody, and I commend her for stepping up when it mattered.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce faces legal vacancy after Daniel McIntyre declines interim city attorney job
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce will have no head city attorney beginning Sept. 11 after former St. Lucie County government attorney Daniel McIntyre turned down the city's offer to serve as interim mu
cards.body:
Fort Pierce will have no head city attorney beginning Sept. 11 after former St. Lucie County government attorney Daniel McIntyre turned down the city's offer to serve as interim municipal counsel. The Fort Pierce City Commission has called a special meeting for 9 a.m. Monday at City Hall to determine its next steps.

The commission voted 2-3 in June not to renew City Attorney Sara Hedges' contract for another year following controversy surrounding the handling of an employee disciplinary matter and claims the city attorney's office was difficult for employees and the public to deal with. Commissioner Broderick cast the lone no vote Aug. 10 when the other four commissioners decided to offer the interim job to McIntyre. Attorney John Anastasio, one-time counsel to former Port St. Lucie Mayor JoAnn Faiella, was the only other person brought to the commission for the interim appointment when McIntyre was selected.

The city is facing a number of potentially complicated legal matters in the upcoming months. A citizen has filed suit against the city over the handling of the leasing of the popular, city-owned Little Jim bar and restaurant property on North Hutchinson Island. Other legal matters could be coming over downtown waterfront projects Crabbys, Fishermans Wharf and Kings Landing.

The commission also is expected to consider Monday signing a contract to pay S. Renee Narlock Associates, a private headhunting firm from Tallahassee, up to $30,950 to recruit and screen applicants to succeed Hedges. The city also used the firm to hire Police Chief David Smith. According to the recruiting contract up for approval Monday, Narlock Associates predicts it could take 16 weeks before Hedges' successor is selected.

cards.headline: Lauderhill man arrested in Treasure Coast Mall jewelry kiosk robbery worth over $22,000
cards.teaser: Dezmone Johnson, 25, of Lauderhill, is charged with robbery and grand theft after allegedly grabbing a tray of necklaces from Royal Jewelers kiosk at Treasure Coast Mall and fleeing the scene on July 20.
cards.body:
Dezmone Johnson, 25, of Lauderhill, was arrested after allegedly stealing more than $22,000 in jewelry from Royal Jewelers, a kiosk inside the Treasure Coast Mall in Jensen Beach, on July 20. Security video from the mall shows Johnson standing at the counter of the kiosk. He actually comes up and pretends to be a customer, engages with the clerk for a few minutes, said Chris Morales of the Martin County Sheriffs Office. According to Morales, Johnson walked away at one point before returning to ask for a closer look at the jewelry. The clerk brings out a tray of, let's say, seven or eight less expensive necklaces according to him, and he just grabs the tray and runs out, Morales said.

The necklaces are valued between $850 and $4,500 each, totaling more than $22,000 in stolen jewelry. Cameras outside the mall showed investigators the vehicle Johnson drove away in. We were able to get the tag from that vehicle, making it pretty easy for us. The vehicle came back to an address in Lauderhill, so down in Broward County, Morales said. Detectives visited a pawn shop near the Lauderhill address and stopped in to ask if Johnson was a customer. Lo and behold, the owner says, 'Yeah, he was just in here trying to pawn a few necklaces.' Again, making it pretty easy for our detectives, Morales said.

Johnson was arrested shortly afterward. Johnson is charged with robbery and grand theft. He spent a short time in the Broward County jail and is currently free on bond as he awaits trial. Morales said Johnson has a history of violence and has access to weapons in his criminal history.

cards.headline: Abandoned boats fill Wildcat Cove near Fort Pierce, creating safety hazards between nature preserves
cards.teaser: Abandoned and derelict boats are accumulating in Wildcat Cove off North Hutchinson Island in Fort Pierce, creating safety hazards and environmental concerns for residents and visitors. The area is located between two nature preserves and is popular for tubing and jet skiing.
cards.body:
Abandoned and derelict boats are filling up Wildcat Cove off North Hutchinson Island in Fort Pierce, creating safety hazards and environmental concerns for residents and visitors. Philipe Chibas, who lives nearby and runs Hot Reels Offshore Adventures, described the area as a "boat junkyard." "Looks like Water World out here," Chibas said. "I have to navigate through this minefield every time I go out with customers."

The boats are located between two nature preserves. The issue follows the city's implementation of a new ordinance limiting boats to anchoring in the water for 45 days before requiring them to be moved. However, Chibas said Wildcat Cove is outside the restricted zone, allowing the problem to persist. "Instead of solving the problem, they pushed the problem somewhere else," he said.

The area is also a popular spot for tubing and jet skiing, and residents are calling for the boats to be removed before an accident occurs. "They should be towed and destroyed," Chibas said. "You cant leave your car on 95." The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission said it has issued several citations and is continuing to monitor the situation.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

hero.headline: Florida SNAP enrollment drops 22% as Trump-backed work requirements take effect
hero.teaser: Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program in Florida fell by more than 22% in a 12-month span as work requirements and other provisions of President Donald Trump'
hero.body:
Enrollment in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program in Florida fell by more than 22% in a 12-month span as work requirements and other provisions of President Donald Trump's big beautiful bill take hold. The state's Department of Children and Families said in a statement that the decreasing number is reflective of the state's strong focus on advancing opportunities for Floridians and their families to achieve economic self-sufficiency. Nationwide, SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2 million in May 2025 to 36.6 million in May 2026, a drop of more than 13%.

The expanded SNAP work requirement now includes adults ages 55 to 64 and those with children ages 14 to 17. Many adults 54 and younger without minor children have long been required to work to get SNAP benefits. The new law requires most people who previously had been exempt from requirements to either work, volunteer or go to school to get benefits. Those 65 and older or with children younger than 14 remain exempt, as do those with health limitations. Some groups that had been exempted from the requirement, including homeless people, no longer are.

Paco Velez, the president and CEO of Feeding South Florida, said the 22% one-year enrollment drop in Florida is driven partly by immigrants who are in the U.S. legally but fear being targeted by Trump's immigration crackdown if they're seeking government benefits. Advocates say people are losing coverage because they miss deadlines or don't have the needed documentation handy, and that some state agencies that run the programs are overwhelmed trying to keep up with changes. Tia Fields, who analyzes social safety net policies at the advocacy group Invest in Louisiana, said the main reason she's seeing people lose coverage is not failure to meet work requirements but administrative paperwork.

The monthly SNAP benefit, which is delivered on debit cards that can be used only for groceries, is $344 per household on average. Children in households that receive the benefit can be automatically enrolled in free school lunch programs or in the SNAP for Women, Infants and Children program for low-income mothers, young children and expectant parents if they meet the other criteria. Some food banks have ramped up donations to try to meet a demand that has risen as SNAP rolls have declined, but advocates say that isn't expected to bridge the gap fully.

hero.headline: James Martin wins Democratic primary for Congressional District 21 by less than 1%, will face Brian Mast in November
hero.teaser: Coast Guard veteran James Martin secured the Democratic nomination for Florida's 21st Congressional District Friday after capturing 50.4% of the vote compared t.
hero.body:
Coast Guard veteran James Martin secured the Democratic nomination for Florida's 21st Congressional District Friday after capturing 50.4% of the vote compared to challenger Bernard Taylor's 49.6%, according to election results from NBC News. The narrow margin underscores the competitive nature of the Democratic race in a district that includes St. Lucie County, Martin County and portions of northern Palm Beach County. Martin will now face incumbent Republican Rep. Brian Mast in November's general election.

Taylor conceded the race Thursday night on social media, acknowledging the outcome while emphasizing the importance of democratic processes. "The voters have spoken, and while this isn't the outcome we hoped for, we respect their decision," Taylor wrote on X. "Democracy only works when we respect the voice of the people, even when the result isn't the one we wanted." Martin posted on Facebook Thursday evening that he was "honored to be the nominee" and congratulated Taylor on a "hard-fought race."

Rep. Brian Mast, an Army veteran who has represented the district since 2017, ran unopposed in the Republican primary. A Democrat has not represented this area of Florida in a decade. Both Martin and Mast bring military backgrounds to their campaigns, with Martin's Coast Guard service and Mast's Army experience potentially resonating with the significant veteran population throughout the Treasure Coast region.

Florida's 21st Congressional District spans a significant portion of the Treasure Coast, encompassing communities from northern Palm Beach County through Martin County and into St. Lucie County. With both major party nominees now confirmed, voters in St. Lucie, Martin and northern Palm Beach counties can expect an active campaign season as Martin challenges the incumbent Republican.

cards.headline: Abandoned boats fill Wildcat Cove near Fort Pierce, creating safety hazards between nature preserves
cards.teaser: Abandoned and derelict boats are accumulating in Wildcat Cove off North Hutchinson Island in Fort Pierce, creating safety hazards and environmental concerns for residents and visitors. The area is located between two nature preserves and is popular for tubing and jet skiing.
cards.body:
Abandoned and derelict boats are filling up Wildcat Cove off North Hutchinson Island in Fort Pierce, creating safety hazards and environmental concerns for residents and visitors. Philipe Chibas, who lives nearby and runs Hot Reels Offshore Adventures, described the area as a "boat junkyard." "Looks like Water World out here," Chibas said. "I have to navigate through this minefield every time I go out with customers."

The boats are located between two nature preserves. The issue follows the city's implementation of a new ordinance limiting boats to anchoring in the water for 45 days before requiring them to be moved. However, Chibas said Wildcat Cove is outside the restricted zone, allowing the problem to persist. "Instead of solving the problem, they pushed the problem somewhere else," he said.

The area is also a popular spot for tubing and jet skiing, and residents are calling for the boats to be removed before an accident occurs. "They should be towed and destroyed," Chibas said. "You cant leave your car on 95." The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission said it has issued several citations and is continuing to monitor the situation.
